sentences: SCC = the sum taken in 64 bits is ≥ 2³², so a bit shifted out of S0 sets it as well as a carry out of the add (RDNA ISA pseudocode: `tmp = (64'U(S0) << N) + 64'U(S1)`).

**Hardware-verified** on the same gfx1100 part through `tools/hw_oracle`: `s_lshl1_add_u32(0x80000000, 0)` = 0 with SCC = 1 (the bit shifted out of S0 sets it, with no carry out of the add), `s_lshl2_add_u32(5, 3)` = 0x17 with SCC = 0, `s_lshl4_add_u32(1, 0)` = 0x10.

Also verified on native RDNA2 (gfx1036, AMD Radeon Graphics): 500 programs in `tools/salu_diff.py` (`--oracle translator,hw`) matched bit-for-bit with 0 mismatches across shift amounts 1–4, confirming that bits shifted out of S0 set SCC as well as sum overflow.
